STEP 1 - Scene: A snack-style plate of cut orange fruit (looks like papaya or cantaloupe/melon chunks) on a white triangular/rounded plate, with a small side dish of almonds at bottom right. Photographed from above at a slight angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white serving plate is roughly 30 cm long along its longest edge; treat it as a ~26 cm equivalent plate. Area = 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2. The almond dish is at the edge and is a separate small dish (~12 cm), so the almonds are included as a second item of the meal only if they are part of this meal; I include them as a small side.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) orange fruit chunks (papaya/melon type), about 10 pieces; (b) almonds in a side dish.

STEP 4 - Area: Fruit covers roughly 22% of the main plate (~117 cm^2). Almonds in side dish cover about 60% of a ~110 cm^2 dish, i.e. ~65 cm^2 (treated separately).

STEP 5 - Volume: Fruit pile height ~2 cm average: 117 cm^2 x 2 cm = 234 ml. Almonds: 65 cm^2 x 1 cm = 65 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Fruit 234 ml x 0.6 = 140 g. Almonds 65 ml x 0.5 (nut bulk density, loose) ≈ 33 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Papaya/melon ~40 kcal/100 g: 140 g → 56 kcal. Almonds ~580 kcal/100 g: 33 g → 191 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 170 g total of fruit and nuts is plausible for a light snack plate of visible pieces; the total of ~250 kcal fits a small snack portion.
